papers.title: Learning Implicit Solves for Dynamic Simulations
papers.summary: High-fidelity simulation of dynamical systems is central to scientific discovery and engineering design, yet remains computationally demanding. Here we introduce the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS), which learns the implicit solve and encodes a time integrator. INOS pretrains a neural operator from static equilibrium solutions and reuses it within Newmark-$\beta$ integration. At each time increment, the integrator forms an effective equilibrium problem, the pretrained neural operator infers the next-step solution field, and the Newmark relations advance the dynamic state. Numerical examples in linear and nonlinear elastodynamics demonstrate accurate full-field predictions without dynamic trajectory supervision. Comparative results show that INOS, evaluated zero-shot, achieves higher predictive accuracy than neural solver baselines trained on dynamic simulations. In addition, INOS delivers over 4,600$\times$ speedup in nonlinear simulations over sequential classical finite-element solvers. INOS natively accommodates changes in dynamic conditions and enables reuse of the pretrained operator across spatial and temporal discretizations. Further evaluation demonstrates a stable million-step rollout. These findings establish INOS as a reusable neural implicit solver for accurate, efficient, and robust dynamic modeling.
papers.title_ja: 動的シミュレーションのための暗黙的解法の学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ニューラルオペレータを用いた暗黙的解法「INOS」を提案する。静的平衡解から事前学習したニューラルオペレータをNewmark-β積分法内で再利用し、動的シミュレーションの各時間ステップにおける解を推定する手法である。線形・非線形弾性力学の例において、動的軌道の教師データなしで高精度な全場予測を実現し、古典的な有限要素法比で4,600倍以上の高速化を達成した。さらに、空間・時間離散化の変更にも対応可能であり、百万ステップ規模の安定したロールアウトも示されている。

papers.title: Adaptive Domain Decomposition for Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.summary: In this work, we present adaptive domain decomposition finite basis physics-informed neural networks (ADD-FBPINNs). The proposed method integrates Partition of Unity Networks (POUNets), a data-driven approach for learning domain partitions, with finite Basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs) to perform more efficient domain decomposition and achieve more accurate approximations. FBPINNs improve upon the accuracy of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) through user-defined subdivisions of the computational domain. By adapting the domain decomposition based on the solution's features using a separable POUNet, the framework can automatically learn partitions that are stable and can be geometrically interpretable. We test this approach on the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation, two-dimensional Poisson equation with multiscale features, and viscous Burgers equation and observe improved accuracy compared with FBPINNs with fixed domain decomposition.
papers.title_ja: 有限基底物理情報ニューラルネットワークのための適応的領域分解
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Partition of Unity Networks (POUNets) を用いて計算領域の分割を自動学習し、有限基底物理情報ニューラルネットワーク (FBPINNs) と統合する手法を提案する。従来の固定領域分解とは異なり、解の特徴に基づいて安定かつ幾何学的に解釈可能な領域分割を適応的に決定することで、精度向上を実現する。ヘルムホルツ方程式、多スケール特性を持つポアソン方程式、粘性バーガース方程式に対する数値実験により、固定領域分解の FBPINNs と比較して精度が改善されることを示した。

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
papers.summary: Neural operators fit their representation of functions to the task they are trained on, so every new task rebuilds a reduced space from labeled data. Following the self-supervised pre-training that made representations shareable in natural language processing and computer vision, we decouple representation learning from operator learning. A functional autoencoder is pre-trained on analytic functions synthesized on the fly, with no solver and no labels, to represent functions on arbitrary point clouds, and the latent space it induces is frozen and reused across tasks. The representation is exactly equivariant to translation, dilation, and amplitude, and reconstructs solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) and natural images on geometries it never saw. Being task-agnostic, the latent space can be interpreted in its own right. The whole space is used and decodes to valid fields, it preserves the ordering of distances between physical fields, its geodesics interpolate physical evolutions, and edit directions transfer across fields. With frozen representation maps, a dataset is encoded once and a neural operator is trained entirely on cached embeddings, which saves memory and training time. On 28 tasks in fluid dynamics, solid mechanics, acoustics, and the Helmholtz and Poisson equations, this paradigm can exceed the accuracy of state-of-the-art end-to-end architectures, with up to an order of magnitude higher throughput and memory savings that fit models nearly two orders of magnitude larger on consumer-grade GPUs. At inference, latent rollouts run up to an order of magnitude faster than regular rollouts, and chunked inference processes functions of over half a billion points on a single consumer-grade GPU.
papers.title_ja: オペレーター学習のための汎用潜在空間の自己教師あり学習
papers.summary_ja: ニューラルオペレーターにおける表現学習とタスク学習を分離し、ラベル不要の関数オートエンコーダーで汎用潜在空間を事前学習する手法を提案する。この凍結された潜在空間は幾何学的変換に対して等変性を保ち、PDE解や画像の再構成に成功する。キャッシュされた埋め込みを用いることでメモリと訓練時間を大幅に削減し、28タスクでSOTAを超える精度と最大1桁の高速化を実現した。推論時にも潜在空間でのロールアウトにより高速処理が可能となり、消費者向けGPUでの大規模モデル運用を可能にする。

papers.title: MIGONet: a multiple-input graph neural operator with solver-free discrete manufactured-solution training
papers.summary: Surrogate modeling of transport requires operators that capture the combined influence of spatially distributed sources and Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, together with training datasets that can be generated at low computational cost. This work presents MIGONet, a multiple-input graph neural operator, and a discrete method of manufactured solutions (MMS) that trains it without solving a partial differential equation, using steady heat conduction as the model problem. In the discrete MMS procedure, temperature fields are prescribed a priori, and the source terms and Dirichlet or Neumann boundary data are evaluated with the same discrete operators as the reference finite-difference method (FDM), so every training sample satisfies the discrete governing equations by construction. Because the boundary data are derived from each field, a Dirichlet or Neumann condition can be assigned to every boundary segment of every sample, and the boundary specification becomes an operator input. MIGONet supplies representations of the complete source field and boundary data to every node before local message passing. On the rectangular domain, it is compared with a version without the complete-source encoder (MIGONet-local) and with the multiple-input operator network MIONet, using the same training data. MIGONet achieves mean relative temperature errors of 10.31% and 10.64% for curved-wire and Gaussian-spot heating, compared with 45.97% and 48.34% for MIONet and 72.25% and 67.82% for MIGONet-local. For 10,000 samples, discrete MMS reduces data-generation time from 486.65 s to 3.15 s relative to matched iterative FDM labeling. Separately trained MIGONet models are also evaluated on L-shaped, disc-shaped, and ring-shaped domains.
papers.title_ja: MIGONet: ソルバー不要な離散製造解法による訓練を行う多入力グラフニューラルオペレータ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、輸送現象のサロゲートモデリング向けに、空間的に分布するソース項と境界条件を同時に扱う多入力グラフニューラルオペレータ「MIGONet」を提案する。従来のPDE求解器を用いたデータ生成の代わりに、離散製造解法（MMS）により計算コストを大幅に削減しながら、離散的な支配方程式を満たす訓練データを効率的に生成する手法を導入した。矩形領域における比較実験では、既存手法MIONetやソースエンコーダなしのモデルと比較し、温度予測の平均相対誤差を大幅に低減した。さらに、L字型や円環状などの複雑な幾何学形状でも、個別に訓練したモデルが有効であることを示している。

papers.title: A trust layer for fast pedestal-stability surrogates: calibrated error bars, out-of-distribution alarms and few-shot recalibration
papers.summary: Machine-learning surrogates of linear peeling-ballooning stability now run in milliseconds, but they are mostly deployed as point estimators: they do not say how wrong they may be, or when a query lies outside what they were trained on. For a fusion company designing a new device, every equilibrium of interest is outside the training data of existing surrogates, so this is the case that matters. We describe a model-agnostic trust layer for stability surrogates, made of conformal error bars, out-of-distribution alarms that route doubtful cases to the physics code, and recalibration from a few simulations of a new design, and we test it with pre-registered hypotheses. On a large public dataset of JET-like equilibria with ideal-MHD growth rates, the error bars hold their nominal coverage in distribution and fall short under a shift in plasma shape; a few dozen simulations of the new shape, or routing the cases the alarms flag, restore it. On resistive BOUT++ surrogates, the bars stay calibrated on held-out runs, the alarm flags tokamaks absent from training, and a scenario scan is screened in seconds instead of hours. Across equilibria from the SPARC library and the DIII-D coil set, a surrogate trained on our own graded BOUT++ labels beats the baseline on unseen equilibria, while a surrogate trained elsewhere ranks the same cases backwards and its alarm declines them. Building our own neural-operator surrogate, the harness exposed two input defects whose fix closed its gap to a simple network. For every surrogate tested, the trust layer keeps coverage near target, with a bar width set by that surrogate's own error. Not every pre-registered hypothesis held, and we report those results and the limits of all of them.
papers.title_ja: 高速ペデスタル安定性サロゲートのための信頼性レイヤー：較正済み誤差バー、分布外アラート、および少ショット再較正
papers.summary_ja: 線形peeling-ballooning安定性の機械学習サロゲートに対し、コンフォーマル誤差バー、分布外（OOD）検知アラート、および少数シミュレーションによる再較正からなるモデル非依存の信頼性レイヤーを提案する。JET類似平衡やBOUT++シミュレーションデータを用いた検証では、分布内では誤差バーが名目カバレッジを維持し、プラズマ形状のシフト下ではアラートが疑わしいケースを物理コードへルーティングすることで信頼性を回復することを示した。さらに、SPARCやDIII-Dのコイルセットを用いた評価では、自社で生成したラベルで訓練したサロゲートが未知の平衡に対してベースラインを上回り、外部訓練モデルの誤りをアラートが正しく検出することが確認された。この手法により、シナリオスキャンの計算時間を数時間から数秒に短縮しつつ、予測の不確実性を定量的に管理できる。

papers.title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
papers.summary: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degenerate nuclear matter, whereas high-fidelity population synthesis connects unknowns in NS formation and binary evolution to large radio-timing surveys. However, repeated structure calculations are prohibitive due to the computational cost of solving the highly coupled partial differential equations of axisymmetric general relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium that govern rotating NS interiors. Non-rotating calculations or approximate rotational corrections can bias equation of state inference and limit the fidelity of population synthesis in tracing the evolutionary history of progenitors and propagating equation of state uncertainties. In this \textit{Letter}, we develop physics-informed neural operators that can solve the axisymmetric problem with high accuracy and negligible computational cost. \textit{Our solvers are trained in a fully unsupervised setting, with the training objective informed solely by the partial differential equations, and achieve a $10^3\times$ speed-up with negligible accuracy loss}. These solvers enable scalable EoS inference that self-consistently accounts for rotation and repeated stellar-structure calculations during binary evolution, making spin predictions that account for rotational structure and EoS uncertainties computationally accessible to population synthesis.
papers.title_ja: 回転する相対論的星のための教師なしニューラルオペレータ：高忠実度の状態方程式推定とパルサーのスピン進化のスケール拡大
papers.summary_ja: 回転中性子星の内部構造を記述する偏微分方程式の計算コストを削減するため、物理情報ニューラルオペレータ（PINO）を開発した。本手法は教師なし学習により、PDEのみを学習目標として用いることで、回転効果を自己整合的に考慮した高忠実度の状態方程式推定を実現する。従来の計算と比較して1000倍の高速化を達成しつつ精度損失はほぼなく、大規模なパルサー集団合成や進化履歴の追跡を計算的に可能にする。

papers.title: To lift or not to lift: Operator inference for nonlinear PDEs with boundary control
papers.summary: Operator inference (OpInf) provides a nonintrusive framework for learning projection-based reduced-order models directly from data, but its standard formulations do not explicitly account for the fact that boundary actuation changes the admissible solution space of a PDE. This paper develops and evaluates a boundary-consistent, lifting-based OpInf formulation for nonlinear PDEs with time-varying inhomogeneous boundary conditions. The proposed approach decomposes the state into a known lifting component that satisfies the prescribed boundary conditions and a homogeneous component represented in a POD basis. Substituting this decomposition into the governing dynamics reveals a boundary-consistent reduced model structure in which the learned dynamics includes bilinear state-input and quadratic input-input interactions for quadratically nonlinear PDEs. The resulting operators are inferred from data, preserving the nonintrusive character of OpInf while guaranteeing boundary condition satisfaction by construction. Numerical experiments on boundary-actuated heat, Burgers, and lid-driven cavity problems show that the lifted formulation improves boundary compliance and can enhance prediction accuracy, solver stability, and computational efficiency, although these gains vary across problems and reduced model dimensions. Overall, this study establishes lifting as a principled extension of OpInf for boundary-actuated PDEs, clarifies when and how this formulation improves performance, and indicates that standard OpInf can remain an effective alternative in certain regimes.
papers.title_ja: 上げるべきか、上げないべきか：境界制御付き非線形偏微分方程式のためのオペレーター推論
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、境界制御付き非線形偏微分方程式（PDE）に対して、リフティング（lifting）手法を用いたオペレーター推論（OpInf）の枠組みを提案する。状態を境界条件を満たす既知のリフティング成分と、POD基底で表現される同次成分に分解することで、境界条件の充足を構造的に保証しつつ、非侵入型の縮約モデルを構築する。熱伝導、バーガース、リッド駆動キャビティ問題での数値実験により、境界適合性、予測精度、計算効率の向上が示された。ただし、効果は問題の種類や縮約次元によって異なり、標準的なOpInfが依然として有効な場合もあることを指摘している。

papers.title: C-GRPO: Conformal Group Relative Policy Optimization
papers.summary: Reasoning-oriented language model training increasingly relies on multiple on-policy rollouts, but standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) uses a fixed group size, wasting compute on easy prompts and under-exploring hard ones. Existing adaptive-budget methods alleviate this inefficiency, yet their stopping rules are heuristic and do not provide a finite-sample calibration guarantee. We propose CGRPO, which replaces the fixed rollout budget of standard GPRO with calibrated conformal thresholds over task-specific nonconformity scores, combining Adaptive Prediction Set (APS)-style calibration for closed-form reasoning, a first-success score for execution-based code, automatic miscoverage selection, and periodic re-calibration. We prove finite-sample coverage for the resulting stopping rule and show that, under monotone policy improvement, recalibration induces a non-increasing expected training budget. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematics, graduate-level science, and code generation, CGRPO reduces mean training rollouts by 49-70% relative to fixed-budget GRPO while retaining strong fixed-budget accuracy, achieves the strongest pass@1 among evaluated static and dynamic baselines on different datasets, and transfers across model families with up to 82% rollout savings.
papers.title_ja: C-GRPO: 同型群相対方策最適化
papers.summary_ja: 推論特化型LLMの学習において、標準的なGRPOが固定のロールアウト数を使用し計算資源を浪費する問題を解決するため、同型予測（Conformal Prediction）に基づく動的な停止ルールを提案する。タスク固有の非適合スコアを用いてキャリブレーションされた閾値を設定し、難易度に応じた適応的な予算配分を実現する。有限サンプルでのカバレッジ保証を証明し、期待される学習予算が単調に減少することを示す。数学・科学・コード生成の6つのベンチマークで、固定予算GRPOと比較して平均49〜70%のロールアウト削減を達成しつつ、精度を維持または向上させた。

papers.title: Agents, Think Only When it Helps
papers.summary: LLM agent distillation transfers agentic capabilities to student models by training on complete teacher trajectories that typically interleave thoughts and actions. We question how critical thought supervision is for agents' ultimate action performance. To answer this, we disentangle their impacts by independently perturbing teacher thoughts and actions during distillation. On widely adopted agent benchmarks across model scales, altering or discarding thoughts has little effect on student performance. We find, however, that thought supervision becomes important when information about the thought is not disclosed in the corresponding action during training. By identifying such discrepant cases, our findings challenge the common practice of distilling entire teacher trajectories for LLM agents, and offer a new insight that thought supervision can be a discernible choice for efficiency depending on whether the information of thought is disclosed in the action.
papers.title_ja: エージェント、役立つときだけ思考せよ
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントの蒸留において、教師モデルの思考（Thought）と行動（Action）のどちらが学生モデルの性能に重要かを解明した。実験の結果、思考情報が行動に明示的に含まれている場合、思考の監督を省略しても性能低下はほとんどないことが判明した。一方、思考に含まれる情報が行動から読み取れない場合のみ、思考の監督が重要であることが示された。この知見は、全軌跡を蒸留する従来の手法を問い直し、効率化のための選択的蒸留戦略を提案するものである。

papers.title: Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference with a small drafter, whose per-guess acceptance rate determines the achievable speedup. Feature-level drafters share a design choice: every token, easy or hard, is drafted under a single forward pass. Many of the tokens the target rejects are ones the drafter is itself unsure about yet the target answers decisively. To address this, we introduce Parallel Reconsideration: guided by its own uncertainty, the drafter reconsiders its hesitant guesses with extra passes that run in parallel with the one-pass draft, adding negligible latency. A co-designed training recipe and serving-time drafting algorithm append these reconsidered guesses to the original draft tree as refined candidates. Across models and benchmarks, on average, Parallel Reconsideration improves over the baselines by 5.3% to 10.2% on acceptance length and by 3.5% to 9.2% on speedup.
papers.title_ja: ドラフターに再考の機会を与える：投機的デコーディングのための並列再考
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMの推論高速化手法である投機的デコーディングにおけるドラフター（下書きモデル）の性能向上を提案する。ドラフター自身の不確実性を指標として、迷っているトークンに対して追加のフォワードパスを並列で実行し、その結果を元のドラフトツリーに統合する「Parallel Reconsideration」手法を導入する。この手法は追加レイテンシをほぼゼロに抑えつつ、ターゲットモデルによる受入率を向上させる。実験により、ベースラインと比較して受入長が5.3〜10.2%、速度向上率が3.5〜9.2%改善することが示された。

papers.title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models
papers.summary: Reasoning models allocate test-time compute across distinct behaviors such as planning, deriving, and verifying. However, models frequently "overthink," continuing to verify and re-derive long after finding a correct answer. This wastes expensive compute and can even degrade performance. Existing interventions, such as token budgets or steering, primarily regulate reasoning duration rather than targeting specific behaviors. In this work, we demonstrate that Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routers provide a natural, training-free interface for behavioral control. We first split reasoning traces into sentence-level segments and label each with one of six reasoning behaviors (planning, execution, restatement, fact, reflection, and conclusion), so that every token carries the behavior of its segment. Linear probes on router logits predict this label nearly as well as probes on the residual stream, the model's full hidden state and the standard target for probing, while using about half as many features. These signals generalize: experts associated with a reasoning behavior on one dataset predict the same behavior on the others, across six datasets spanning five domains (math, code, science, knowledge, and commonsense). Building on this, we selectively edit expert router scores during inference to curb overthinking. Across four models and four benchmarks, this intervention reduces the number of generated tokens by a median of 30.4% (and up to 63.3%). Crucially, it encourages the model to stop once the problem is solved, rather than skipping essential reasoning steps. Accuracy never drops by more than 0.5 percentage points, and frequently improves. Ultimately, MoE routing offers both an interpretable lens into reasoning states and a lightweight mechanism for optimizing test-time compute.
papers.title_ja: 推論の経路：MoEモデルにおけるテスト時計算の読み取りと再構成
papers.summary_ja: 推論モデルが正解後も検証を繰り返す「過剰思考」による計算資源の浪費を解決するため、MoE（Mixture-of-Experts）のルーティング信号を活用する手法を提案する。ルーティングのロジットに線形プローブを適用することで、推論の各段階（計画・実行・検証など）を高精度に識別できることを示した。推論時に特定のエキスパートのスコアを選択的に編集することで、過剰な検証を抑制しつつ、精度を維持または向上させる。4つのモデルとベンチマークで、生成トークン数を中央値で30.4%削減しながら、精度低下を0.5ポイント以内に抑えることを実証した。

papers.title: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
papers.summary: RL for LLM reasoning often reaches an early performance plateau as the policy distribution becomes increasingly sharp. Recent work has studied policy entropy as both a diagnostic and a control signal for this behavior. In our experiments, however, increasing entropy alone does not reliably change the eventual plateau. We analyze RL through its implicit target policy and derive a sharpness factor $\kappa$, together with an effective counterpart $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}$, that describes how strongly reward or advantage gaps are translated into probability-ratio gaps. Motivated by this view, we introduce \emph{reward budgeting}, a plug-in advantage construction that assigns a fixed total reward budget to each prompt. For binary rewards and independent on-policy rollouts, its unclipped score-function estimator follows the gradient of an exact finite-$G$ concave objective with diminishing returns, while its advantage gap decreases as more rollouts become correct. For general rewards, a shifted log-mean interpretation holds asymptotically under the stated regularity conditions. These results motivate, rather than establish exact objective equivalence for, the clipped implementations. On Qwen3-8B and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, reward budgeting consistently improves a range of RL baselines, with gains up to +12.50 on AMC23 and +10.00 on AIME24 and AIME25. Overall, our results support an update-dynamics view of premature convergence and show that strong gains can be obtained without explicitly preserving entropy.
papers.title_ja: 報酬予算付けによるLLM推論における強化学習の早期収束低減
papers.summary_ja: LLMの推論能力向上に向けた強化学習（RL）において、ポリシー分布のシャープ化による早期性能頭打ち（プレマチュア・コンバージェンス）を解決する手法を提案する。従来のエントロピー制御では効果が限定的であるため、報酬やアドバンテージのギャップが確率比のギャップにどれだけ変換されるかを記述する「シャープネス係数」を導出する。これに基づき、各プロンプトに対して固定の総報酬予算を割り当てる「報酬予算付け」手法を導入し、有限サンプル下での凹目的関数の勾配に従うことを理論的に示す。Qwen3-8BやLlama3.2-3B-Instructを用いた実験では、AMC23やAIME24/25などの数学ベンチマークで最大+12.50点の改善を確認し、エントロピーを明示的に保持せずに性能向上が得られることを実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論のRL最適化と効率化、ベンチマーク評価に直結する高度な手法

papers.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
papers.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead. In this work, we systematically study the HC architecture to understand its components and identify simpler, more efficient designs. We find that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates form two effective interaction groups: either alone achieves performance comparable to mHC. We also identify repeated access to the expanded residual state as a major source of training overhead, even without mixing. These findings lead to SimpleHC, which simplifies the architecture by removing residual mixing and simplifies execution through shared memory access, using the resulting additive structure and shared gate inputs. Layer-specific gates share a group-entry state, enabling batched reads and deferred writes; scalar corrections exactly preserve preceding sublayer output contributions. Our analyses support both the retained residual structure and the design of shared memory access. SimpleHC incurs only 2.4% extra end-to-end training time over a vanilla residual baseline at the largest tested scale. It maintains performance comparable to mHC when scaling from 15B to 30B MoE models, exhibits smoother gradient dynamics during standard training, and remains stable under stress. We hope SimpleHC will encourage a broader pursuit of simplicity in foundation model design, making performance gains more accessible and practical at scale.
papers.title_ja: ハイパーコネクションの設計について：簡素化、安定性、スケーラビリティ
papers.summary_ja: フロンティアLLMで採用が進むハイパーコネクション（HC）アーキテクチャの構成要素を体系的に分析し、より簡潔で効率的な設計を提案する。学習済みゲートと固定ゲートの組み合わせが性能維持に重要である一方、拡張残差状態への反復アクセスが訓練オーバーヘッドの主因であることを特定した。これに基づき、残差混合を除去し共有メモリアクセスを用いた「SimpleHC」を設計し、バッチ読み書きとスカラー補正により計算負荷を低減した。最大規模のテストでは、バニラ残差ベースライン比で訓練時間をわずか2.4%しか増加させず、15B〜30B MoEモデルで同等の性能と安定した勾配動態を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの効率化・推論高速化・大規模モデル設計の核心を扱うため

papers.title: Data-Efficient Scaling-Law Discovery for Recommendation Systems via Coupled Hyperparameter Scaling
papers.summary: Large-scale ranking and recommendation models of Web platforms benefit from increased compute much as large language models do, and their scaling behavior is broadly power-law in form. Yet ranking models have heterogeneous architectures which makes their scaling law less straightforward than that of LLMs. We address how to discover the scaling law of an arbitrary ranking model efficiently. We introduce a scaling layer, which groups primitive architecture parameters into semantically coherent groups and defines how they co-vary, inducing a mapping from a low-dimensional space of hyper-hyperparameters into the full architecture space. On top of it, Axia fits scaling-informed surrogates, selects configurations by a posterior-based acquisition criterion, and returns a Pareto frontier from which per-model operating points are validated -- replacing exhaustive sweeps with a small number of informative runs. A fleet-level evaluation protocol, computed on a fixed representative model set under matched trial budgets, makes refinements to either component measurable. Our contribution is an automated system that learns model-specific complexity-quality relationships and gives uncertainty-aware guidance for allocating compute across a heterogeneous model ecosystem. Across 34 model iterations in two development cycles on Meta's ads ranking and retrieval system, the workflow yielded a mean 0.66% offline normalized-entropy improvement and 0.36% cumulative online lift.
papers.title_ja: 結合ハイパーパラメータスケーリングによるレコメンデーションシステムのデータ効率の良いスケーリング則発見
papers.summary_ja: Webプラットフォームのランキングモデルにおけるスケーリング則を効率的に発見する手法を提案する。アーキテクチャパラメータを意味的にグループ化し、低次元空間から高次元空間へのマッピングを行う「スケーリングレイヤー」を導入した。さらに、スケーリング情報を活用したサロゲートモデルと後方確率ベースの獲得基準を用いることで、網羅的な探索を避け、少数の実行でパレートフロンティアを導出する。Metaの広告ランキングシステムでの評価により、オフライン・オンライン双方で性能向上が確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルとベイズ最適化による計算効率化が関心に合致

papers.title: RAGAM-AI: A Hybrid Reinforcement Learning based Agentic approach powered by Generative AI for Edge Resource Management
papers.summary: Resource management for distributed edge networks hosting different services has been handled efficiently using Reinforcement learning (RL). Reward generalization in complex workflows is still an open issue within the RL realm. Therefore, this work proposes RAGAM-AI, a hybrid framework that combines the capabilities of RL algorithms and Generative-AI (Gen-AI) for powering an Agentic AI workflow that optimizes resource allocation at the Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) units. This framework further resolves the reward generalization issue by utilizing Large Language Model (LLM) for feedback. A Multi- Agent Soft-Actor Critic (MASAC) using Math{\Sigma}tral as a reward oracle is implemented for managing resource allocations at the MEC. RAGAM-AI interprets system state information and evaluates multi-objective trade-offs guiding the resource orchestration loop over distributed edge server agents. The complexity of the framework is further brought down by incorporating surrogate reward model. The overall performance is evaluated against the single agent SAC, REINFORCE and random policies for benchmarking. On using RAGAM-AI, lower allocation deviations for CPU, memory and bandwidth resources are reported while minimizing the latency and data rate costs. A scalable AI as a feedback (AIAF) solution optimizing network resources with significant performance improvement is thus presented.
papers.title_ja: RAGAM-AI: 生成AIを活用したハイブリッド強化学習ベースのエージェントアプローチによるエッジリソース管理
papers.summary_ja: マルチアクセスエッジコンピューティング（MEC）におけるリソース配分最適化を目的とした、強化学習（RL）と生成AI（Gen-AI）を統合したハイブリッドフレームワーク「RAGAM-AI」を提案する。LLMを報酬オラクルとして活用することで、複雑なワークフローにおける報酬汎化の問題を解決し、マルチエージェントソフトアクタークリティック（MASAC）アルゴリズムを実装している。さらに、サロゲート報酬モデルを組み込むことで計算複雑性を低減し、CPU・メモリ・帯域幅の配分偏差を低減しつつレイテンシとコストを最小化する性能を、単一エージェントSACやREINFORCEと比較して実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: RLとLLMの統合、サロゲートモデル活用、エージェント設計が関心に合致

papers.title: Context--Answer Metamodels: Forecasting LLM Activations Before the First Answer Token
papers.summary: Under stochastic decoding, a single context can elicit many different answers from a language model. Characterizing this variation typically requires many expensive autoregressive rollouts, each revealing only one realization. We ask whether the activations produced while reading the context can directly forecast the model's rollout activations. We train context--answer metamodels that map a context activation sequence to point or distribution forecasts of mean-pooled answer activations. We find that (i) the four metamodel families we study forecast mean-pooled answer activations with high fidelity, and the distribution metamodels also capture rollout variability; (ii) performance improves as the training set grows to 500,000 prompts, and the metamodels generalize zero-shot to out-of-domain datasets; (iii) their forecasts retain behavior-predictive signal; and (iv) context activations from Qwen2.5 predict mean-pooled answer activations from Qwen3.5 and Gemma 4, suggesting that activation forecasts can transfer across models. Together, these results suggest that context activation traces can support scalable forecasts of behaviors in LLM answers before the first answer token is generated.
papers.title_ja: コンテキスト-回答メタモデル：最初の回答トークン生成前にLLMの活性化を予測する
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMがコンテキストを読み込んだ際の活性化状態から、実際の回答生成時の活性化を予測するメタモデルを提案する。4つのメタモデルファミリーを用い、平均プーリングされた回答活性化を高精度に予測できることを示し、分布メタモデルがロールアウトのばらつきも捕捉できることを確認した。さらに、50万プロンプトでの学習により性能が向上し、ドメイン外データへのゼロショット汎化や、Qwen2.5からQwen3.5/Gemma 4への活性化予測の転移可能性を実証している。これにより、最初の回答トークン生成前にLLMの挙動をスケーラブルに予測する手法が提供される。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの内部状態予測と効率化に直結する手法

papers.title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
papers.summary: We develop a physics-informed method for aerodynamic shape optimisation of turbine blades, treating the flow field and blade geometry as coupled unknowns. The method translates prescribed surface-pressure distributions into geometric modifications through pressure-target continuation and alternating flow-geometry updates. A differentiable representation of the blade surfaces allows their positions and orientations to be optimised within the current flow field, followed by flow re-adaptation to the modified boundaries. The inverse formulation uses the two-dimensional steady compressible Euler equations as physics constraints and is evaluated on the LS89 turbine cascade using 28 pressure-target points derived from experimental data. Starting from a modified profile and a warm-started flow network, the final pressure-side and suction-side root-mean-square fitting errors are 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure, respectively. Independent forward verification with SharC reproduces the principal surface-pressure trends of the experimental measurements, with remaining differences near the trailing edge. These results demonstrate the translation of experimental-origin loading data into geometric blade modifications through coordinated optimisation of the flow field and moving boundaries.
papers.title_ja: 圧力駆動型タービンブレード最適化のための物理情報ニューラルネットワーク手法
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、タービンブレードの気動力形状最適化において、流場とブレード幾何学を結合した未知数として扱う物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）手法を提案する。指定された表面圧力分布を幾何学的修正に変換するため、圧力ターゲット継続法と流場・幾何学の交互更新を行う。2次元定常圧縮性オイラー方程式を物理制約として用い、LS89タービンカスケードで実験データ由来の28個の圧力ターゲット点を用いて評価した。結果、吸気側と排気側のRMS誤差はそれぞれ入口全圧の1.13%と2.21%となり、独立した前方検証でも実験測定との主要な圧力傾向を再現した。
papers.relevance_reason: PINNと最適化の組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に直接該当する。

papers.title: Improving Hydrofoil Efficiency Through Simulation-Driven Design Optimization
papers.summary: Foil windsurfing is a sport in which competitors fine-tune their setup to optimize performance under varying environmental conditions. However, such adjustments are typically guided by intuition. This paper presents a methodology for improving hydrofoil design using computational fluid dynamics. First, structured light scanning was used to obtain the geometry of a conventional hydrofoil. Subsequently, five derived designs have been explored, inspired by advancements in airplane wing design. Following this, a preliminary design was selected, and a design of experiments approach was implemented. Generated simulation data were used to train a machine learning surrogate, which is ultimately used in the multi-objective design optimization. While the surrogate-based approach yielded promising results, it was limited to exploring a restricted set of design parameters. To overcome this constraint, additional improvements were attained through adjoint optimization, demonstrating that comparable performance can be achieved with a distinctly different hydrofoil design. Finally, the conventional design was refined through adjoint optimization. Notably, adjoint optimization yielded a 15% increase in efficiency. The results suggest that both proposed approaches can produce novel hydrofoil designs capable of outperforming the original configuration under specific conditions; however, due to its inherent flexibility, the adjoint approach with realistic constraints offers more freedom in the design exploration process.
papers.title_ja: シミュレーション駆動型設計最適化による水翼効率の向上
papers.summary_ja: CFDシミュレーションと機械学習サロゲートモデルを用いた水翼設計最適化手法を提案する。実験計画（DOE）で生成したデータから訓練したサロゲートを用いた多目的最適化に加え、隣接法（adjoint optimization）による設計探索も実施した。隣接法を用いることで、従来の設計に対して15%の効率向上を実現し、サロゲートアプローチよりも柔軟な設計空間の探索が可能であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルと隣接法による最適化は、ユーザーの関心である「サロゲート支援最適化」と「物理情報・数値計算との融合」に強く関連する。

papers.title: KolTa: A Physics-Informed Active Learning Framework for Formulation Discovery with Limited Data
papers.summary: Finding high-performing formulations is difficult when few have been measured and experimental budgets are limited. We propose KolTa, an active learning framework that selects batches to discover the top 5% of formulations at a target temperature under a fixed query budget. KolTa combines a three-stage predictor of component contributions, role-conditioned interactions, and anchored temperature response with task-specific soft physics constraints. Its Physics-Residual-Calibrated Upper Confidence Bound (PRC-UCB) acquisition rule combines predicted utility, ensemble disagreement, and a target-temperature physics residual, with nonnegative exploration weights fitted to out-of-fold signed errors. We evaluate the framework on three measured tasks and one simulated task covering binary-mixture viscosity, drug solubility, ionic-liquid viscosity, and electrolyte conductivity. KolTa ranks first or second in mean area under the learning curve (AULC) on every task and outperforms seven of the eight comparator strategies in paired tests, winning 75 of 78 paired comparisons across tasks and seeds against those seven strategies. Across the three measured tasks, its largest gap to the best mean AULC is 0.032, compared with at least 0.056 for every comparator. On Drug, reaching 80% average recovery of the remaining targets across drugs requires an estimated median of 348 additional formulation queries, about 18% fewer than the fastest comparator. Researchers can adapt the framework to diverse formulation problems through component roles and physical constraints.
papers.title_ja: KolTa: 限られたデータでの処方発見のための物理情報アクティブ学習フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 限られた実験予算下で高性能な処方（混合物）を効率的に発見するための物理情報アクティブ学習フレームワーク「KolTa」を提案する。成分の寄与、役割条件付き相互作用、温度応答を段階的に予測し、物理的制約をソフトに組み込むことで、物理残差を考慮した獲得関数（PRC-UCB）を実装した。粘度、溶解度、イオン液体粘度、電解質伝導率の4タスクで評価し、既存手法と比較して学習曲線下面積（AULC）で上位を維持し、特に薬剤溶解度タスクでは比較対象より約18%少ないクエリ数で目標達成を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報とベイズ最適化の組み合わせが関心に合致

papers.title: Microdroplet Generator Surrogate Enhancement and Inverse Design Through an Uncertainty-Guided Framework
papers.summary: Microfluidic droplet generation is critical for many applications, yet efficient device design in high-dimensional parameter spaces remains computationally prohibitive due to complex multiphase flow dynamics. This work presents a unified methodology that couples adaptive surrogate enhancement with simulation-driven inverse design. High-fidelity Volume-of-Fluid simulations provide ground-truth data, while neural network ensembles predict flow regimes and droplet diameters. Ensemble-based uncertainty quantification identifies epistemic uncertainty using consensus levels for regime classification and the coefficient of variation for diameter prediction, revealing that uncertainty concentrates near regime transition boundaries where physics is highly sensitive to parameter perturbations. A physics-informed enrichment strategy targets these critical zones and addresses class imbalances by deploying additional targeted simulations and retraining the surrogates forming the ensembles. A framework that integrates Particle Swarm Optimization for constrained inverse design, balancing accuracy with predictive confidence and physical consistency is therefore proposed. Validation on independent test datasets demonstrates that the enriched ensembles achieve higher accuracy, with the fraction of predictions within the 0-3% error range on droplet diameter nearly doubling, and high-error cases (above 10%) dropping substantially. The inverse design procedure reliably identifies physically realizable configurations meeting target droplet sizes. This approach significantly reduces computational costs while ensuring reliable predictions, offering a framework with potential applicability to the optimization of a broad range of microfluidic systems.
papers.title_ja: 不確実性ガイド型フレームワークによるマイクロドロップレット生成器のサロゲート強化と逆設計
papers.summary_ja: 高次元パラメータ空間におけるマイクロ流体デバイスの設計を、適応型サロゲートモデルと逆設計の統合により高速化する方法を提案する。ニューラルネットワークアンサンブルを用いた不確実性定量化により、物理的に敏感な境界領域を特定し、そこにターゲットシミュレーションを追加する物理情報ベースの補強戦略を実行する。さらに、粒子群最適化（PSO）を用いた制約付き逆設計フレームワークを構築し、予測精度と信頼性のバランスを最適化する。検証の結果、ドロップレット直径の予測誤差が大幅に低減され、計算コストを削減しつつ物理的に実現可能な設計を効率的に特定できることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデル、不確実性定量化、逆設計の統合が関心に合致

papers.title: Amortized Optimization for Calibrating Stochastic Social Simulators
papers.summary: Stochastic simulators need suitable parameter values to reproduce observed behaviour in complex systems. Searching for these values through repeated simulations makes frequent recalibration computationally expensive. We develop an amortized optimizer that uses simulations collected in advance to learn how to choose parameters that make simulated outcomes agree with observations. Once fitted, it maps new observations to feasible parameters without further simulator calls. The method retains alternative parameter settings that can explain similar observations and compares their responses, avoiding the conflicting labels that arise when training a single parameter regressor. Historical observations also provide supervision by showing which simulated responses agree with the data, even when the underlying parameters are unknown. Experiments across four simulators compare calibration accuracy and query time. Dedicated cost analyses quantify traffic preparation and the recorded financial reuse costs.On new traffic targets, local correction more than halves query time relative to empirical and surrogate selection; a learned inverse is faster still, with similar mean error. In a retrospective comparison on real financial data, our method returns parameters about $1.07\times10^{7}$ times faster than a 10-minute Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization search, with mean calibration error 3.06% higher. Reusing simulation work across observations supports repeated parameter updates when the available time is too short for a new search.
papers.title_ja: 確率的社会シミュレータのキャリブレーションのための償却最適化
papers.summary_ja: 確率的シミュレータのパラメータ調整（キャリブレーション）において、反復シミュレーションによる計算コストを削減する償却最適化手法を提案する。事前に収集したシミュレーションデータを用いて、観測値からパラメータを直接推定するモデルを学習し、新たな観測時には追加のシミュレーションなしでパラメータを特定する。単一のパラメータ回帰では生じるラベルの競合を回避し、類似の観測を説明し得る複数のパラメータ設定を保持する。金融データを用いた比較実験では、ガウス過程ベイズ最適化よりも約1000万倍高速にパラメータを返却し、キャリブレーション誤差はわずかに高いものの実用的な精度を維持した。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルとベイズ最適化の高速化が関心と一致

papers.title: PINR-ESI: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Implicit Neural Representation Framework for EEG Extended-Source Imaging
papers.summary: EEG extended-source imaging aims to localize active cortical regions and characterize their spatial extent, yet supervised inverse networks typically depend on synthetic EEG-source pairs and may be sensitive to synthetic-to-real mismatch. We propose a physics-informed self-supervised implicit neural representation (INR) framework for spatial source reconstruction without paired source labels or simulation-based supervised pretraining. The lead field matrix encodes the source-to-sensor volume-conduction model and constrains the INR through agreement between predicted and measured EEG. Cortical current density is modeled as a continuous coordinate-conditioned field. A classical inverse estimate provides warm initialization and spatial constraints on source activity, while patch-integrated projection maps the field to discrete source coefficients for forward modeling. Simulations with varying noise levels, source counts, and source extents showed the clearest advantage in identifying active cortical regions, particularly for multiple and larger sources. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations using real EEG recordings from epilepsy patients and intracranial stimulation experiments further supported the feasibility of the framework for source imaging. These findings suggest the potential of physics-informed self-supervised INR for extended-source imaging.
papers.title_ja: PINR-ESI: 脳磁図（EEG）拡張ソースイメージングのための物理情報セルフスーパーバイズド暗黙ニューラル表現フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、EEGによる脳内活動源の空間的再構成において、教師データやシミュレーション前提の事前学習に依存しない物理情報セルフスーパーバイズド手法を提案する。リードフィールド行列を用いた物理的制約と、座標条件付き連続場としての暗黙ニューラル表現（INR）を組み合わせることで、実測データと予測値の一致を最適化目標とする。古典的逆問題解によるウォームスタートとパッチ統合投影により、離散ソース係数へのマッピングを効率化し、ノイズやソース数・範囲が異なるシミュレーションで特に複数・大規模ソースの同定精度向上を示した。てんかん患者の実測EEGおよび頭内刺激実験による評価を通じて、実臨床応用における有効性を検証している。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットとサロゲートモデルの応用が関心に一致

papers.title: Energy-Guided Transport for Projection-Free Physics-Informed Flow Matching
papers.summary: Deep generative models, particularly Flow Matching frameworks, have emerged as powerful tools for synthesizing complex physical systems. However, standard architectures remain purely statistically driven and agnostic to the underlying governing equations, often violating fundamental physical constraints during inference. Existing zero-shot approaches designed to enforce these constraints typically rely on rigid algebraic projections. While effective for sparse boundary conditions, applying such discrete geometric corrections to dense, full-domain PDEs may disrupt the probability path, \rev{potentially deviating from the learned manifold and introducing substantial computational overhead}. To address these challenges, we introduce Energy-Guided Transport, a novel training-free framework that formulates non-linear physical constraints as a smooth potential energy landscape. Rather than interrupting the ODE integration, our method applies a continuous dissipative force directly to the intermediate generative states, steering them toward the physical manifold. By evaluating this force implicitly via reverse-mode automatic differentiation, our framework preserves the natural dynamics of the flow while maintaining an efficient $\mathcal{O}(N)$ algorithmic complexity. We extensively evaluate our framework across various 1D and 2D physical systems, including the chaotic Navier-Stokes equations. Our method achieves stable generation without structural divergence, significantly improves the stability-accuracy trade-off compared to state-of-the-art methods, and substantially accelerates inference with respect to exact projection strategies. Code available at: https://github.com/ispamm/Projection-free-energy-guided-flow-matching.
papers.title_ja: 射影なし物理情報フローマッチングのためのエネルギー誘導輸送
papers.summary_ja: 物理法則を無視しがちな生成モデルに対し、離散的な射影ではなく滑らかなポテンシャルエネルギー景観を用いて物理制約を強制する新しいフレームワークを提案する。ODE積分中に連続的な減衰力を適用することで、学習されたマニホールドから逸脱せずに物理的に妥当な解へ誘導する。逆モード自動微分を用いることで計算効率を維持し、ナビエ・ストークス方程式などの複雑な系で安定性と精度の両立を実現した。

papers.title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming with Derivative-Free Configuration Search
papers.summary: Generalized disjunctive programming (GDP) describes process design alternatives with Boolean variables, disjunctions, and logical propositions, and fixing one configuration leaves a subproblem in the continuous variables. Conventional GDP methods require explicit equations, which a simulator may not expose, and mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) reformulations can be intractable for nonconvex models. The external-variable reformulation turns configuration choice into an optimization over an integer lattice whose objective is the subproblem value, which derivative-free optimization (DFO) can search while the GDP model continues describing the alternatives. We pair GDP models with surrogate DFO methods and the direct-search method NOMAD and compare them with discrete steepest descent (D-SDA), logic-based and MINLP solvers, and enumeration on nine process models, 21 test functions, a pharmaceutical flowsheet simulated in PharmaPy, and a catalytic distillation column with 100,947 configurations. On the largest reactor network, the surrogate methods MISO and RBFOpt reach the reference in nine or ten of ten runs with about 30 subproblem solves, whereas logic-based methods solve nearly one subproblem for each admissible configuration and most D-SDA descents end at one local minimum. In the flowsheet example, where GDP solvers do not apply, RBFOpt and MISO find the best of 36 simulated configurations in every run with 20 evaluations. For the catalytic column, D-SDA and MISO reach the best known design with 100 evaluations, whereas MINLP solvers find no design within 15% of it and global solvers return contradictory certificates. This search pays off when the configuration space is too large to enumerate, has deceptive local minima, or has MINLP reformulations that fail, and enumeration or a direct reformulation is simpler for small algebraic models.
papers.title_ja: 導関数フリー構成探索を用いた汎化離散プログラミング

papers.title: Data-Driven Stochastic LQR Control with Probabilistic Guarantees and Uncertainty Refinement
papers.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for the direct, data-driven synthesis of the stochastic linear- quadratic output-feedback control for linear systems sub- ject to process and measurement noise. Using delayed input-output measurements, we derive a lifted parameter- ization together with an equivalent lifted linear quadratic cost, enabling controller synthesis without explicitly identi- fying the lifted dynamics. Two complementary closed-loop formulations, based on trajectory and covariance represen- tations, are then developed, whose uncertainties depend only on the realized but unknown lifted noise. We char- acterize the relative performance of the two formulations in finite-data regimes. High-probability uncertainty bounds are developed for realized noises, leading to a convex optimization solution to the problem, whose feasibility cer- tifies probabilistic mean-square stability (p-MSS) and per- formance guarantees. To reduce conservatism, Gaussian zonotopes are used to refine uncertainty sets by elimi- nating noise realizations inconsistent with measured data, and a novel intersection rule enables the consistent fusion of data-driven and physics-informed information. These components are integrated into an adaptive framework that unifies indirect (identification-based) and direct (control- oriented) data-driven linear-quadratic output-feedback con- trol. Unlike existing direct data-driven LQR methods that verify stability a posteriori, our by-construction approach achieves robust stability alongside reduced conservatism and superior performance. Simulation results show that the proposed controller approaches the ideal optimal solution while outperforming existing data-driven methods under noisy measurements.
papers.title_ja: 確率的保証と不確実性の精緻化を備えたデータ駆動型確率LQR制御

papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
papers.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted. Unlike classical workflows with fixed graphs, the aggregate compute, bandwidth, and end-to-end latency demands of such pipelines are unknown at dispatch time: they emerge at runtime from intermediate observations and stochastic token sampling, yielding heavy-tailed, multi-modal random variables. This unpredictability forces infrastructure orchestrators into a dilemma: under-provisioning risks mid-execution throttling and deadline violations, while over-provisioning wastes scarce edge or cloud capacity. Existing schedulers require a fully known pipeline graph, while edge resource-management methods rely on parametric or stationary demand models, and neither fits the unknown, non-stationary profiles of agentic pipelines. We formalize this setting as the uncertainty-aware agentic orchestration problem, where the goal is to reserve, at dispatch time, compute and bandwidth allocations that cover actual pipeline demands, and to verify that the pipeline can meet its deadline, each with a prescribed probability. We then propose Conformal Reservation for Orchestration (CRO), an online algorithm that translates a sliding window of past execution traces into dispatch-time resource allocations with finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees via conformal prediction. Simulations over heterogeneous task mixes with multi-modal and heavy-tailed profiles show that CRO is the only evaluated method that simultaneously satisfies target probabilistic coverage across all risk levels while, among coverage-feasible methods, attaining the lowest over-reservation, roughly halving the resource waste of the Chebyshev-bound baseline.
papers.title_ja: エージェント型AIシステムのための不確実性考慮リソースオーケストレーション

papers.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.summary: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We argue that a key limitation is that existing systems select experts and retrieve knowledge from the question alone, rather than from gaps that emerge during reasoning. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps. These signals trigger targeted knowledge retrieval or mid-discussion specialist recruitment. On the MEDAGENTSBENCH hard subset (862 questions across nine biomedical datasets), upfront retrieval provides little benefit, while challenge-aware in-between retrieval performs better; on a multi-specialist backbone it improves accuracy on 8 of 9 datasets and adds 6 percentage points over Challenger Only. Ablations indicate benefits from both retrieval timing and gap-specific query signals, and a live web-search experiment shows that the timing advantage persists across retrieval backends. For specialist recruitment, self-triggered adaptation is unreliable, whereas Challenger-triggered recruitment raises GPT-4.1-mini MedQA accuracy from 46% to 54%, with positive direction on all tested generalization datasets. Naively combining retrieval and specialist recruitment degrades performance, highlighting the need to coordinate adaptive intervention channels. These results show that when and why external resources are recruited is a key design choice in multi-agent medical reasoning.

papers.title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
papers.summary: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with several objectives, such as helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty, typically relies on preference judgment for each objective, growing the annotation cost linearly with the number of objectives. Active preference learning can reduce this cost by selecting the comparisons whose labels are expected to change the policy most. Existing remedies either lack an objective-aware query selection mechanism for the multi-objective setting or regard conflicting preferences as harmful, therefore excluding them from the training data. We introduce OGC-DPO (Objective-conditioned Gradient Coverage DPO), an active learning framework that treats each (response pair, objective) combination as a separate query and measures its informativeness through the policy's own implicit gradient, without relying on an external reward model. OGC-DPO then selects the queries that most expand each objective's gradient coverage. Empirical experiments across varying numbers of objectives demonstrate the effectiveness of OGC-DPO over existing active preference learning methods under the same annotation cost. Further analysis demonstrates that informative conflicts, rather than being uniformly harmful, provide a useful policy training signal.
papers.title_ja: 多目的アライメントのための目的条件付き能動的嗜好学習
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の多目的アライメントにおいて、アノテーションコストを削減する能動的嗜好学習フレームワーク「OGC-DPO」を提案する。各目的ごとの勾配カバレッジを最大化するクエリを選択することで、外部報酬モデルに依存せずに情報量の高い比較データを効率的に選定する。実験により、既存手法より少ないコストで性能を向上させることを示し、対立する嗜好データも学習シグナルとして有効であることを明らかにした。

papers.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
papers.summary: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret text but lack numerical precision, while Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are quantitatively accurate but cannot reason about the effects of text. Moreover, the lack of large-scale paired multimodal datasets limits progress in bridging this gap. In this work, we address this challenge by providing a scalable approach for generating realistic multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs. Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. We align the two models in stages, first fine-tuning the LLM via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward tied to covariate-induced improvement in forecasting performance, and then fine-tuning the TSFM on covariates generated by the aligned LLM. Our experiments show that models trained on our synthetic multimodal corpus generalize to real benchmarks spanning finance, economics, weather, traffic, and security. Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o. Code, checkpoints, and the evaluation datasets are publicly available.
papers.title_ja: TSFMとLLMの融合：コンテキストを共変数として

papers.title: LACS: Distribution-Sensitive Label-Agnostic Confidence Selection for Dynamic Data Pruning
papers.summary: Training on large datasets motivates selecting which examples receive expensive training computation. Fixed quotas determine the amount of pruning in advance, while absolute confidence cutoffs depend on the score scale. We study a population-relative alternative that adapts the threshold and retained count together. We introduce LACS (Label-Agnostic Confidence Selector), a training-time rule based on maximum predictive confidence, requiring neither labels at selection time nor per-example gradients. LACS removes examples at or above a log-mean-exp reference plus a margin. We characterize its sensitivity to score gaps and mass, and derive an exact no-pruning condition. For $0<\rho<1$, the removed fraction is at most $\rho$ and at least one example remains. The unsigned score permits both confidently correct and confidently wrong examples to be removed. Seven evaluation settings include neural training, language modeling, and boosting. Neural execution studies reduce backward-active rows by 10-35%; on CIFAR-10, 29% fewer backward rows accompany accuracy means of 89.77% versus 89.82% for full CE. At a matched backward budget and number of optimizer updates, LACS is 1.0 pp above small-batch training and 1.2 pp above random selection over five seeds. Across 14 tabular datasets, quadratic boosting reduces mean test error from 23.36% to 22.96%. Its full training replays use about 30% fewer fitting rows; these counters span a different horizon from validation-selected accuracy. In one RBF-SVM case study, elapsed time falls by 37% with slightly lower error. These findings separate selective-work reduction from realized acceleration: the current exact-current-score neural implementation uses an additional scoring forward, so its backward sparsity does not yet translate into wall-clock acceleration. This overhead is an execution choice rather than a requirement of the selection rule.
papers.title_ja: LACS: 動的データプルーニングのための分布感応型ラベル非依存信頼度選択
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、学習時の計算コスト削減を目的とした動的データプルーニング手法「LACS」を提案する。ラベルや勾配を必要とせず、予測信頼度の分布に基づいて閾値を適応的に調整し、過学習や誤った高信頼サンプルを効率的に除去する。CIFAR-10や言語モデルなど7つの評価設定において、バックワード計算の行数を10〜35%削減しながら精度を維持または向上させることを示した。ただし、現在の実装ではスコアリング用のフォワードパスが追加されるため、壁時計時間（実測時間）の高速化には至っておらず、計算量削減と実効速度向上の乖離を指摘している。

papers.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
papers.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on external memory stores to retain information across conversations, typically via dense vector embeddings searched with approximate nearest-neighbor methods. The fruit fly's olfactory circuit computes a locality-sensitive hash of sensory input using a strikingly different mechanism - sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition - and prior work (Dasgupta et al., 2017) showed this scheme, dubbed FlyHash, preserves neighbor structure better per bit than conventional random-hyperplane hashing (SimHash) on several benchmarks. We apply FlyHash, to our knowledge for the first time, to LLM agent memory retrieval, and ask three questions a practitioner actually needs answered: does the quality advantage hold under a correctly matched-bit protocol (it does, robustly, across 10 seeds and four datasets spanning two modalities, with one specific, previously undocumented comparison pitfall identified and corrected along the way); does that advantage translate into real memory and latency savings, including against the dense-vector indexing (HNSW) practitioners default to today (no: at equal bits FlyHash's codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash's, and HNSW dominates both hash methods at ordinary scale; a sparse-set comparison we introduce recovers most but not all of a naive latency gap, leaving hashing's practical case narrower and more specific than the quality result alone implies); and does the advantage survive genuine, non-circular agent-memory relevance labels rather than the nearest-neighbor-by-embedding proxy this literature otherwise relies on (it does). We report all three answers precisely, including the two that narrow rather than flatter the headline result, and release our implementation, a working agent-memory demo, and a full account of the methodological pitfalls we found and corrected.

papers.title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
papers.summary: Firms using large language models under fixed budgets must decide which model to call and whether to retry a failed task. Because a call's charge is revealed only after completion, one long response can exhaust the remaining budget and leave later tasks unserved. Our objective is to maximize the number of tasks solved before service stops. We develop a contextual bandit policy, ADP-HT, which learns each model's task-specific success probability and constructs conservative cost estimates from coarsened response-length labels on a quantile grid with $2^K$ intervals. The policy weighs predicted success against these costs, adjusting the cost penalty to realized spending and the budget available per remaining task. Under calibration, local regularity, and grid-coverage conditions, we bound the excess allowance in the policy's conservative cost estimates. At a fixed sample size, increasing $K$ reduces the discretization term but increases the estimation allowance. At the tightest tested budgets, ADP-HT solves more than twice as many MATH500 and GPQA tasks as the best implemented baseline. It achieves the highest mean cumulative score at ten of fourteen RouterBench budgets. On LiveCodeBench, it outperforms a deployed commercial router in both default and cost-saving modes at the three lowest test budgets.
papers.title_ja: パスワイズ・バジェット付きLLMルーティング：Kビット尾部コスト学習によるオンライン割り当て

papers.title: PEARL: Prediction Error-Adaptive Regularized Learning for Selective Forgetting under Partial Preference Drift
papers.summary: User preferences shift as needs, context, and tastes evolve. This matters for personalized recommendation, LLM response generation, and RLHF-trained reward models, which can become miscalibrated as preferences drift. Existing non-stationary bandit methods forget uniformly across all dimensions, but real preference shifts are typically partial: some dimensions go stale while others remain valid. Neural contextual bandits accumulate confidence monotonically via the Gram matrix, with no mechanism to direct uncertainty where predictions have gone wrong. We propose PEARL (Prediction Error-Adaptive Regularized Learning), which reverses the Gram update along feature directions where predictions are surprisingly wrong, while leaving confidence intact elsewhere. We prove that (i) any non-adaptive policy suffers linear regret after a preference shift, (ii) no fixed exploration rate achieves low regret in both stationary and non-stationary regimes, and (iii) PEARL's cumulative regret scales with the number of shifted users N_s, not the total population N. On PRISM, a personalized LLM response selection benchmark (1,500 users, 21 LLMs), PEARL beats greedy by +4.0 points and the best neural bandit baseline by +2.5 points (p<0.001), while performing on par with greedy when preferences are stable. It beats sliding-window and discounted approaches by 3 to 10 points, showing that selective forgetting outperforms uniform forgetting. The selection policy is a ~100K-parameter MLP that runs in milliseconds on CPU, leaves LLM weights frozen, and works with any API-based model.
papers.title_ja: PEARL: 部分的な嗜好ドリフト下での選択的忘却のための予測誤差適応型正則化学習
papers.summary_ja: ユーザーの嗜好変化に対し、全次元で均一に忘却する従来の手法の限界を指摘し、予測誤差が大きい特徴量方向のみ信頼度を低下させる「選択的忘却」手法PEARLを提案する。理論的に、非適応型ポリシーは線形リグレットを被ることを証明し、PEARLがシフトしたユーザー数に比例してリグレットが縮小することを示した。LLM応答選択ベンチマークPRISMにおいて、既存のニューラルバンディットベースラインを上回る性能を達成し、CPU上でミリ秒単位で動作する軽量なMLPポリシーとして実用性を備えている。
